title: WPSB/322/2023 of DR BIKRAM CHAND SHAH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
SRI JUSTICE VIPIN SANGHI, C.J.
AND
SRI JUSTICE RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
JULY 21, 2023
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 322 of 2023
Between:
Dr. Bikram Chand Shah .............Petitioner

And
State of Uttarakhand and others .........Respondents
Counsel for the appellant: Mr. Mayank Rajan Joshi,
learned counsel for the petitioner
Counsel for the respondent: Mr. Vikas Pande, learned
Standing Counsel for the State /respondents.
Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Court made the following
JUDGMENT: (Per Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

1. By the present writ petition, the petitioner is
praying for the following reliefs:
"I. Issue a writ mandamus quashing the
impugned Office Order dated 23.06.2023 bearing
number 539(I)/XXIV-C-4/2023-03(03)/2023
(ANNEXURE 4), qua petitioner.
II. Issue a writ of mandamus or any other
appropriate writ, order, or direction declaring
Section 7 (d) and Section 17(2)(d) of the
Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for Public Servants
Act, 2017 as void and inoperative for being ultra
vires Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.

2
III. and/or pass further order/s as may be
deemed fit and proper in the facts and
circumstances of the case."
2. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner was
inducted in service as an Assistant Professor and joined, as
such, on 15.07.2005 and at present, is serving as Professor
(B.Ed.) at Government P.G. College, Gopeshwar in District
Chamoli. It is further pointed out by the petitioner that he
has served in the remote areas for more than 17 years and is
still willing to serve in the remote areas. It is further pointed
out by the petitioner that in the last academic sessions, the
respondents transferred the employees from remote area to
accessible areas and subsequently, the employees, who were
transferred in the previous sessions were granted an
exemption from transfer for three years vide Office
Memorandum dated 31.05.2023, the copy of which is
appended to the writ petition as Annexure-2. Apart from
this, the petitioner submits that he is taking care of his ailing
mother, who happens to be an Octogenarian and is totally
dependent upon the petitioner and it is difficult for his
mother to adjust the life in plains. The petitioner in the
petition has enclosed the copy of the eligibility list for transfer
of employees uploaded on the website of the Department,
which is appended as Annexure-3 to the writ petition,
wherein the name of the petitioner is placed at Serial No. 1,
which is a list prepared as per Section 12 of the Uttarakhand
Annual Transfer for Public Servants Act, 2017 (The Act No.
01 of 2018), for compulsory transfer from remote area to
accessible area.
3. The petitioner submits that he specifically requested
the Department not to transfer him from Gopeshwar and the
request thus made by the petitioner is ignored by the
respondent-Department in the list prepared as per Section 12

3
of the Uttarakhand Act No. 1 of 2018. Vide impugned order
dated 23.06.2023, 34 teachers have been transferred on the
recommendation of the Transfer Committee constituted as
per Section 16 of the Act as aforesaid from remote areas to
accessible areas. The persons who were transferred by the
said Office Order dated 23.06.2023 are those incumbents
who were categorised under the compulsory transfer. In this
Office Order, the name of the petitioner is placed at Serial No.
1, whereby the petitioner has been transferred from the
Government P. G. College, Gopeshwar (Chamoli) to
Government P.G. College, Kotdwar (Pauri Gahrwal). Being
aggrieved with the transfer pursuant to the main Office Order
dated 23.06.2023, the petitioner represented to the
respondent-State by way of a representation dated
03.07.2023, a copy of which is annexed as Annexure-5 to the
writ petition, wherein he submits that some of the teachers
were permitted to retain in remote areas on their requests
and though, he also request to retain in a remote area but he
has been transferred to Government P.G. College, Kotdwar.
Apart from this, in the representation, he gave a reference
that twice he was attached though during entire service
tenure no disciplinary proceedings were ever been initiated.
He further gave a reference in the representation that though
he was attached in Government P. G. College, Pithoragarh, he
approached to the High Court and the order of attachment
was suspended and the matter is still sub judice and pending
in the High Court. To this representation, in fact, the
petitioner is asking the same treatment, whereby the other
teachers were retained in the remote areas.
4. By relief no.2, the petitioner is seeking a
declaration that Section 7 (d) and Section 17 (2) (d) of the
Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for Public Servants Act, 2017
be declared as void and inoperative being ultra vires to Article
14 and 16 of the Constitution. In reference to this relief, the

4
petitioner submits that the respondent-department has
operational control on 116 Degree Colleges within the State,
out of which, 85 colleges are categorised as the colleges
located in remote areas and rest 31 colleges as in accessible
area and this figure reveals that 73.27% colleges are in
remote areas and the remaining 26.73 % of collages are in
accessible areas, which create inherent problem not only to
the department itself but it is also for the employees as well
as the students. It is further contended that since under the
provisions of Uttarakhand Act No. 01 of 2018, the teachers
completing 10 years of service are entitled to get exemption
from transfer from accessible areas to remote areas which
creates anomalous situation. The petitioner in reference to
the said averments prepared a District wise tabulation of
remote posting and accessible posting in para 3 of the writ
petition.
5. The petitioner further submits that since as per the
categorization as done by the Department, 2/3rd of the
institutions are categorised as located in the remote areas
and if the employees receiving the protection under Section
7(d) of the Act for transfer from accessible area to remote area
an anomalous situation would arise where an employee is not
available to serve in the remote areas and this is only
because of the exemption granted under section 7 (d) (iii) of
the Uttarakhand Act No. 01 of 2018.
6. The another contention, which has been raised by
the petitioner in the petition is that an employee serving in
the State knows the geographical condition of the State and is
well aware of the fact that the State of Uttarakhand has a
total geographical area of 51.125 Sq.Km. and of its total
geographical area 47,325 Sq. Km. is covered by mountains,
while 3800 Sq. Km. is Tarai plains and by calculation the
State has mountains terrain in 92.5 % of its geographical

5
area and the rest 7.57% is plain and the employees opting to
serve in the State very well know that they are bound to be
transferred to any place within the State, and as a matter of
right they cannot be placed at their own choice. The
description of geographical area as given by the petitioner, is
based upon research, the reference of which has been given
in the petition, as follows:
 "Meena H R, Ram H, Singh S K, Mahapatra R K,
Sahoo A and Rasool T.J 2007: Animal husbandry
practices at High altitude (>6000 feet) in Kumaon region
of Uttarakhand, India. Livestock Research for Rural
Development. Volume 19, Article # 163. Retrieved July
13, 2023, from http:// www.Irrd.org/ Irrd 19/11/meen
19163.htm."
7. The petitioner in the petition in order to
demonstrate that the provisions of Uttarakhand Act No. 01
of 2018 is nothing but an act of discrimination amongst the
employees based on their place of posting since, one set of
employees get protection from compulsory transfer and
others do not. The Tabulation Chart, as mentioned in the
petition, is being extracted herein below:

8. On the basis of the table, as above, the petitioner
submits that Section 7 (d) of the Act accords preferential
treatment to the employees posted in accessible areas
whereas the employees serving in the remote area have not
provided a same or similar protection or treatment. As such,
the act does an artificial classification between the employees

7
on the basis of their place of posting wherein members of
same class of services are treated differently.
9. In order to challenge the vires of Section 7(d) of the
Act, the petitioner submits that the petitioner rendered more
than 17 years of service in a remote area but since the
exemption is not available to the petitioner since he is posted
in remote area, he cannot ask for such exemption from
transfer. Consequently, the petitioner submits that the act of
respondent is nothing but a hostile discrimination
perpetuated by the respondents as the persons similarly
situated are treated differently. Due to this hostile
discrimination, the petitioner is seriously prejudiced since the
protection from compulsory transfer is not available to the
teachers posted in remote locations and this differently
treatment has no reasonable nexus to the object sought to be
achieved by the Act.
10. Before further discussion, certain provisions of the
Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for Public Servants Act, 2017,
are being reproduced herein below:
"Section 6. There shall be following kind of Annual transfer, namely: -
(a) Compulsory transfer from accessible area to remote area;
 (b) Compulsory transfer from remote area to accessible area; and
 (c) Transfer on the basis of request.
Section 7. There shall be following norms for compulsory transfer from accessible
areas to remote areas; namely: -
(a) The employees, who is posted for 04 years or more at present place of
posting in accessible area shall be compulsorily transferred subject to the
number of vacancies available and anticipated under section 10 in remote
area;
(b) The employees, who are working for less than 04 years at present
place of posting in accessible area but during whole service period have served
in accessible area for more than 10 years, shall also be compulsorily
transferred from accessible area to remote area subject to availability of
vacancies/posts in remote area as above:
 Provided that for the counting of total service period in accessible area
the proviso of definition of accessible area given in Appendix specified in
section 3 of this Act shall also be taken into consideration;
(c) The employee being transferred to remote areas from accessible areas
shall compulsorily be transferred to accessible area again on completion of

8
minimum period prescribed for posting in remote areas and the date of their
reliving from remote areas shall be clearly mentioned in their transfer order
also;
 (d) The employees under following categories shall exempted from
compulsory transfer from accessible area to remote area; namely: -
(i) Senior employees;
(ii) Such employees who have already completed minimum 10 years
service in remote areas, and;
(iii) The employees seriously ill/disabled under section 3 and who
submit a certificate from competent authority.
(iv) Such spouse whose only son/daughter is included in definition of
disability;
(v) Spouse of employees posted in military and Para military force.
Section 10. There shall be following norms for compulsory transfer from remote area
to accessible area; namely: -
(a) The employee who is posted for 03 years or more at the place of their
present posting in remote areas shall be compulsorily transferred to accessible
area.
(b) If any employee is working for less than 03 years at their present place of
posting but have served in remote area during whole service period for more
than 10years, shall be compulsorily transferred from remote area to accessible
area. To determine such period, the proviso of definition of remote area
mentioned in Appendix specified under section 3 shall be taken into
consideration:
 Provided that while counting this period only such period shall be
counted during which the employee was actually working in the remote area,
if he is attached to accessible area, then period of attachment in accessible
area and the period of leave excess to one month in a year shall not be
counted for the purpose of calculating the period of posting in remote area.
Section 11. The maximum ceiling of compulsory transfer from a remote area to
accessible area shall be as follows; namely: -
(a) The compulsory transfer from a remote area to accessible area shall
be made upto a limit of total vacancies available and anticipated under section
7 in accessible area in concerned cadre. The counting of eligible employees for
transfer shall be done in order of period of total service rendered in remote
area during whole service period;
(b) Such employees who are posted for more than 03 years at their place
of posting or rendered services for more than 10 years, during the whole
service period in remote area shall be identified for transfer in descending
order according to the total period of posting in remote area in their whole
service period upto the limit of availability of vacancies in accessible area."
11. On close scrutiny of the aforesaid provisions of the
Act and taking into consideration that the petitioner rendered
more than 17 years of service in a remote area, the petitioner
falls under the category of compulsory transfer since the
period, on which, he has rendered in remote areas is more
than 10 years. Respondent-Department in the present

9
transfer session of 2023-24, prepared a list as per the
mandate of Section 12 of the Uttarakhand Act No. 01 of
2018. Now, for ready reference, Section 12 of the Act No.01 of
2018 is being reproduced here in below:
 "12. A list of employees eligible for compulsory transfer from remote area
to accessible area shall be prepared. By publishing/circulating vacancies
available and anticipated in accessible areas, option shall be invited from the
eligible employees for maximum 10 desired places. It shall be compulsory for
the employees to give his opinion in preferential order. Vacancies and list of
employees eligible for transfer shall also be displayed in the website of
Uttarakhand."
12. The list so prepared is enclosed in the petition,
wherein the name of the petitioner is at Serial No. 1 and as
per the list, the petitioner has rendered 17 years 10 months
and 17 days in remote areas. This list further gives reference
in column 11 that the petitioner is not interested though as
per Section 12 of the Uttarakhand Act No. 01 of 2018, it is
mandatory for an employee to give his option for transfer.
Merely on the ground that the petitioner has not opted and
has no desire of transfer from a remote area, the petitioner
cannot question the transfer on the ground that since he has
not opted, therefore, he cannot be transferred from remote
area to accessible area. As it appears from the Uttarakhand
Act No. 01 of 2018, the maximum ceiling of compulsory
transfer from a remote area to accessible area are clearly
mentioned in Section 11 and since the petitioner is posted in
a remote area for more than 17 years and as such, the
petitioner completed the maximum ceiling period even more
than the maximum ceiling period of posting in remote areas
and by virtue of Section 11, the petitioner falls under the
category of compulsory transfer. It is mandate of Section 12
that the petitioner should opt for transfer but it appears from
the list prepared under Section 12 of the Uttarakhand Act No.
01 of 2018, that the petitioner deliberately has not opted.
Once, Section 12 clearly provides that if an employee is

10
eligible for compulsory transfer from remote areas to
accessible area, he should compulsorily exercise the option
for transfer but the petitioner has not opted and such an
action of the petitioner in not exercising his option of transfer
from the remote area to accessible area is totally in flagrant
violation of the mandate of Section 12.
13. The submission of the counsel for the petitioner
that there is a hostile discrimination amongst the employees
posted in a remote area and accessible area, since, the
exemption are only meant for the employees posted in
accessible area, is not acceptable. The exemption so granted
under Section 7 (d) are only meant for certain class of
employees, who either are senior employees or suffered from
serious illness or disabled or their spouses are included
under the definition of disability or the spouse of employee
posted in military and Para military force, therefore, they fall
in different classes and, as such, the classification has a
reasonable nexus to the object sought to be achieved by
Section 7 (d) of the Act. Further submission of counsel for the
petitioner in reference to Section 17(2)(d) are also not
acceptable as exemption from transfer are meant for a
different class.
14. In view of the observations as above, since the
petitioner rendered more than 17 years of services in remote
places and in view of the provisions of the Uttarakhand
Annual Transfer for Public Servants Act, 2017, the petitioner
falls under the category of compulsory transfer and, as such,
we do not find any illegality in transferring the petitioner by
the order impugned. Apart from this, the transfer is an
exigency of service and the petitioner has no vested right to
remain posted at one place. We are not inclined to interfere
with the impugned transfer order so far as it relates to the

11
petitioner. Hence, the Writ Petition being devoid of merit is
dismissed.
 No order as to costs.
